records.words: A lantern going dark is a nice small mystery to start with. I like that it is one question, not a lore page.
A lovely warm lantern and Sam wanting to watch me find the fault. The guide says carry it, so I will, and I want to see it go dark myself.
It went dark, just like they said. A quarter of an hour for one test. Now I want to look inside.
Four parts in a little circuit. It works on the table and dies when moved, so I am guessing something is loose. Contact sounds like the loose thing.
Looking closely at the contact.
Aged and dull, a hint but not proof. The guide now wants me to measure from the battery while carrying. Fine, I will follow it rather than guess.
Red on A, as the picture says.
6.00 volts at the battery while carried, so the battery is fine. The guide moves me along step by step; I like that it reads like a little detective trail, though I wanted to test my contact guess.

Six volts across the switch, so it opens when shaken. It is the switch, not my dull contact. I was wrong, and the meter told me so plainly; that is a readable consequence. But the guide did the thinking.
It says examine before changing anything. Replace would be the lazy answer and uses my only switch, so I will look first.

The guide says fit a replacement, but the outside is intact and it is my only spare. I want to try adjusting it first; maybe it is just loose inside. That is the unusual reply, and I want to see if the game lets it matter.
Tightened again, it says. Again? Someone has done this before. Testing.
Still dark. My adjustment did not fix it, or not enough. The guide sends me back to the battery, which feels like starting over; I would rather check the switch again myself.
I like that it marks the old reading as taken before the latest work. Probes are still on the switch, so I will read again there instead of the battery.

Just after sixty seconds. I am finding why a lantern goes dark when carried, with Sam watching. The meter, probes, carry and repair buttons are clear. I guessed the contact, the meter said the switch. I tried adjusting instead of replacing my only switch; it still drops six volts across the switch while carried, so my gentler fix failed. Each action costs game minutes on a 9-to-5 bar. I like the readable trail; I have not heard from Sam since the start.
All right, I give in and use my only switch. The cracked spare lantern stays whole for now; I did not want to break one thing to fix another.
Bright and steady. Oh, it is Sam’s mother’s lantern. I want to see whether she or Sam notices that I tried the gentle fix first.

Fixed, on time, a family favour for nothing. Her line about carrying it to the garden table is sweet but short, and nobody mentions my adjust attempt. Sam went quiet after the first line. I want to look at People.
Nora’s grandmother’s music box, and she does not want new parts. That is the one I care about. Rafi is from Bornova, like the Turkish names elsewhere. I want to ask Nora first.
Look at an object together first. Fair, I asked too early. I will find the music box on the board.
The music box card is below the bottom bar. Scrolling to reach it.
Accepting the music box. Three identical Accept promise buttons, so I am tapping the one on her card.
Opening the music box on the bench.
Spring, gear, governor, drum. It wants 15 turns a minute while working harder. I want to hear it sound wrong first.
The drum barely turns, the tune is unrecognisable. The guide has gone quiet, which I actually like. Now that I have looked at her box, I want to ask Nora about it.
Nora chose to tell me about the work, but her words are folded away. Opening them.

I asked about the music box and she told me about a handle sketch, her brother’s repair, an exhibition, an accessible grip. That is a real confession, and I like that she trusted me, but it has nothing to do with her grandmother’s music box. I am not sure what object she means, and there is nothing I can say back.
Without the guide I will try the same method as the lantern: measure along the chain and find where it drops.
The meter is set to Carry from the lantern; the box needs Work harder. Switching.
Across the spring first.
150 turns per minute difference across the spring. I have no idea if that is good. It says compare with Notes, so I will look.
The normal speed must be under Reference.

Oh, this is a real little puzzle. Spring 150 is right. Divide by 5 for the gear: 30. Governor at setting 2 keeps it 30, drum halves it to 15, exactly what Nora wants. So I should measure at the governor and see what the ring is doing. I like doing the arithmetic myself.
After the governor it should be 30 if the ring is right.
7.5 instead of 30. A quarter. No ring setting gives a quarter, so either the gear is slipping or the governor is stuck. I will measure at the gear to split them.

It is 7.5 already after the gear, where it should be 30, so the gear is the culprit and the governor is innocent. I worked that out myself from the reference, and that felt really good. Nora asked for no new parts, so I want to fix this gear rather than swap it.
Looking at the gear before touching it, like the lantern taught me.

Intact outside again, same as the switch. That tells me nothing. Last time adjust did nothing, so this time I will try cleaning; old music boxes get gummed up, I think. Keeping her grandmother’s gear.
Residue on the teeth! That sounds like the real thing. Testing.
Same speed. Cleaning removed residue but did not help. I will try adjusting before I give up on her original gear.
Cleaned and reseated, still the same. The only thing left is replacing the gear, and she said no new parts. I do not want to decide that for her. I want to ask Nora.
The Ask Nora button is gone now. Maybe What Nora said has something about the box.
Same handle-sketch story, no way to ask her about the gear. Sam wanted to see how I find the fault; maybe he has an idea.

Share an actual observation with Sam first. But I have measured the box four times and cleaned and adjusted the gear. How do I share an observation? I do not see a button for that. I am stuck between replacing a gear Nora asked me not to replace and a meter that says the gear is wrong.
Checking the i button for how sharing works.
The i panel is about Sam’s goodwill and time, not how to share an observation. Closing.
The help panel followed me to the bench and changed to Finding the fault. Closing with the corner ×.
Maybe the little arrow by the box name lets me ask Nora or put it aside.

I know what I want: to tell Nora the gear is worn and ask whether she will accept a new one. There is no way to ask her. Her sheet repeats no new parts, the people page repeats the handle sketch, and Sam wants an observation I do not know how to share. I would close it here, or replace the gear and feel I went behind her back.
There is a Recent conversation fold in her sheet. One more look before I decide.
Third time I have read the handle sketch. Nothing about the music box. Closing.
The wish has not passed. Looking at the menu before I leave.
I am stopping fits. Selecting it locally; I will not type or submit anything.

I am stopping at 13:40 on day one with Nora’s music box on the bench. I fixed the lantern, and working out from the reference that the gear was the culprit was the best moment. But cleaning and reseating did nothing, the only fix left is a new gear she asked me not to use, and I could not ask her. I would not leave it running. I would come back another evening if I could talk to Nora about the gear, because I care how that box ends. I am stopping is selected locally; I typed nothing and pressed no Submit.
